html:
The Arab revolt in Palestine was an uprising of Palestinian Arabs against British rule and Jewish immigration, from 1936 to 1939. It began with a general strike and grew into a rural guerrilla war.

Jewish immigration had surged after the Nazis came to power in Germany. Arabs feared losing their land and country under the British mandate. In 1937 the British Peel Commission proposed, for the first time, to partition Palestine into two states.

Britain crushed the revolt with tens of thousands of troops, mass arrests, house demolitions and executions; about 5,000 Arabs were killed, and Arab leaders were exiled. In 1939 Britain's White Paper sharply limited Jewish immigration. The broken Arab leadership was weak in the war of 1948 (Nakba). See also Zionism.
sum: The Arab revolt in Palestine was an uprising of Palestinian Arabs against British rule and Jewish immigration, from 1936 to 1939. It began with a general strike and grew into a rural guerrilla war.
